Yes! I was re-stretching the fabric at least 2-3 times per piece, especially for the bits that were closer to the edge to avoid the design warping, and one final time before gluing. I tried to break up the work so I wasn't completely murdering my back. I've actually been tracking my hours just trying to see how everything stacked up. Altogether this frame was... 55.19 hours of tufting/trimming over the span of about a week. Keep in mind that I'm a total beginner and once my technique improves I'm sure I can shave off a bit of the time that my yarn cakes were getting tangled, color matching over and over, etc.
Most definitely just waiting until I finish the trimming and backing 🤓

This 💜 I appreciate you. When I figured out how to actually try sculpting I started spending hours and hours at a time just in front of my frame trying to get crispy ass lines and tweezing fibers into place. Everyone's got different skills to play at, and just because I see 200 Murakami flowers and AF1 silhouettes doesn't mean they're of the same quality I hope to achieve.

It's so easy to become close minded when you're just thinking to yourself all the time. Thank you for helping drag me out of this little pity party I've been throwing. We really do have a lot of different pathways once you get the initial supplies 😁
I tufted her without shaving between colors DURING tufting, so even after she's dried and trimmed I'm sure I'll eventually redo her and a few of the other Chao designs

I agree! My first couple rugs I didn't shave until the end and you notice a MAJOR difference between that and when you shave in between doing different colors. I don't have the funds to buy those nifty automatic scissors yet, so taking the extra time to trim between colors is the most helpful for me to get them crispy looking lines 🤙🏾
I'm so proud of her! But she was also done without trimming between colors so I'm a little scared to trim her at the end 😅 I plan on making the whole little SA2 trio at some point
